court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: PLRA exhaustion timing relative to original complaint
issues.why: Court must decide whether exhaustion is measured at the original complaint's filing when Carter had not completed the grievance process.

issues.label: Amended complaint curing exhaustion defect
issues.why: Whether a plaintiff can cure an initial failure to exhaust by exhausting before filing an amended complaint.

issues.label: Persuasive weight of unpublished Hardin decision
issues.why: The court relied on an unpublished Fourth Circuit case whose precedential authority and correctness must be assessed.

issues.label: Exhaustion of First Amendment retaliation claims
issues.why: Whether the retaliation claims first raised in the amended complaint were properly exhausted through the September 2022 grievances.

issues.label: Exhaustion availability when grievances rejected at intake
issues.why: Whether intake rejections rendered the grievance process unavailable, excusing further exhaustion under Ross v. Blake.

issues.label: Failure to file regular grievance after Branch rejection
issues.why: Whether Carter's abandonment of the June 2022 complaint at informal stage defeats exhaustion of the reentry/retaliation claim.

issues.label: Exhaustion as affirmative defense/burden
issues.why: Defendants bear the burden of proving non-exhaustion, which affects summary judgment propriety.

issues.label: Summary judgment before discovery
issues.why: Whether granting summary judgment prior to any discovery was premature given factual exhaustion disputes.

issues.label: Supervisory liability standard against Clarke
issues.why: Whether Carter alleged Clarke's knowledge of and deliberate indifference to Carter's specific conditions to state supervisory liability.

issues.label: Frivolity dismissal standard under §1915A
issues.why: Whether the court properly applied screening standards in dismissing the Clarke claim.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment conditions-of-confinement merits
issues.why: Whether RHU conditions analogous to Porter v. Clarke state a constitutional violation, especially given Carter's mental illness.

issues.label: First Amendment retaliation elements against Branch
issues.why: Whether protected activity, adverse action, and causal connection are adequately alleged.

issues.label: Retaliation claims against McCoy and Cabell
issues.why: Whether Branch's secondhand references sufficiently implicate the wardens in retaliatory conduct.

issues.label: Whether informal complaints constitute protected activity
issues.why: Court must determine if filing informal complaints/grievances is First Amendment protected conduct.

issues.label: Mootness of injunctive relief after transfer
issues.why: Carter's release from Sussex may moot claims for injunctive relief regarding those conditions.

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment immunity for Commonwealth
issues.why: The Commonwealth of Virginia is generally immune from §1983 damages suits and is not a 'person.'

issues.label: Qualified immunity for individual defendants
issues.why: Officials may be immune from damages if the rights were not clearly established.

issues.label: Pro se liberal construction of pleadings
issues.why: Carter's filings must be liberally construed, affecting sufficiency determinations.

issues.label: Relation-back of amended complaint
issues.why: Whether the amended complaint relates back to the original filing date under Rule 15(c).

issues.label: Scope of claims not addressed on merits
issues.why: Defendants did not address Eighth Amendment merits, limiting what the court may resolve.

issues.label: Damages availability absent physical injury
issues.why: PLRA §1997e(e) may limit mental/emotional damages without physical injury.
